title: Splitting a homogeneous reacting solution preserves fractional kinetics
title_de: Aufteilen einer homogenen Reaktionslösung erhält die relative Kinetik
question: Does an aliquot react at the same fractional rate as its larger remainder?
script:
# KI-005: Splitting a homogeneous reacting solution preserves fractional kinetics
# Design only: predictions below are not measured observations.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 H2O2 0.001mol
add v1 catalase 0.000001g
wait 5s
new
decant v1 v2 0.25
inspect
wait 20s
inspect
expected_result: If enzyme and substrate transfer proportionally, both portions retain the same concentrations and should show similar fractional peroxide depletion, while absolute consumption scales with volume.

expected_processes.interpretation: Educational equation or schematic relationship; not a claim that every species, pathway or coupling is implemented.

acceptance_checks.criterion: Verify proportional enzyme and substrate transfer before comparing rates.
Compare fractional loss from each post-split starting amount, not equal absolute gas amounts.

novelty.basis: A new experimental question or substantive controlled extension; not a novel scientific discovery or necessarily a new reaction family.
novelty.distinction: Tests intensive versus extensive reaction-rate scaling after representative aliquoting.
novelty.original_147_note: Original catalogue reviewed as source context through web excerpts; no complete local automated comparison or semantic-novelty certification.

limitations: The enzyme is an effective surrogate and must remain dissolved; unresolved phase transfer makes the comparison inconclusive.
safety_context: Simulation-only script. Not a wet-lab procedure, school risk assessment or permission to perform the chemistry.
